sealed.statement: For every current authoritative readiness planning generation, the ReadinessPlanningSnapshotOwner either publishes a completed snapshot for that generation or explicitly supersedes it with a newer generation, so continuous source churn never leaves its consumers (the critical-topology settling gate and routing readiness) indefinitely served by planning_snapshot_refresh_pending. The planning owner holds the single definition of generation currency (generation/token, rebuild admission, completed snapshot, completed-snapshot reuse, supersession); consumers never decide freshness themselves and callers never mint planning generations. Invariants: (SAFETY) a completed snapshot is never reused after a semantic dependency of its generation changed — a mutation that ignores generation mismatches must red; (LIVENESS) if the authoritative planning state stops changing at generation G then, within bounded owner work and without any wall-clock timeout as the bound, the completed snapshot's generation == G and planning_snapshot_refresh_pending clears; (SUPERSESSION) during continuing churn each obsolete build may be superseded, but the owner mints no additional semantic generation without an authoritative cause — a mutation that rotates the generation continuously must red; (OWNERSHIP) the topology settling gate and routing consume the owner's readiness contract and do not independently judge snapshot freshness; (ENGAGEMENT) under production-shaped post-formation churn on the seed (five nodes, moving clock) the seed's own completed snapshot becomes and stays reusable between authoritative changes, with a red-on-revert proof; (LIVE) on the local docker formation fixture the seed's critical-topology settling gate stops reporting node_ready_lease_incomplete for nodes whose readiness facts are unchanged, and routing no longer reports all_services_filtered_by_readiness for the seed, against the 601x / 175x settle-waits measured on GCP e9774db2e and locally. Scope owns ONLY the ReadinessPlanningSnapshotOwner generation/admission/reuse contract and its single clock-domain input for generation semantics; it does NOT own the critical placement planner, storage_reservation_reconcile, the projection-readiness evidence owner (A3, closed), routing policy, or the settling gate's consumption policy.

claim: MEASURED (3 local docker formation runs, seed, planning-owner probe): the seed process holds 52 ReadinessPlanningSnapshotOwner instances — owner#1 (bootstrap control-plane-setup) serves 100% of reads; owners #2-#52 are private ControlPlaneReadinessService instances constructed per hosted partition by unified-rebalancer-lifecycle-base.js:251 (partition-service-rebalancer-methods.js:223 injects no controlPlaneReadinessService), each subscribing to cache changes and rebuilding every node's planning snapshot per table change (51 x ~1,131 = 57.7k duplicate rebuilds, 52x cache-change fan-out, 52x token maintenance) while serving zero reads.

MIXED-CLOCK HYPOTHESIS FALSIFIED as a material driver: direct latch probe over 330 s — 365,484 calls (229k numeric, 136k ISO-fallback), 483 refreshes, 35 backwards refreshes, 319 key changes (0.97/s; 306 at >=250 ms, 12 at <250 ms, 10 attributable to the backwards/mixed domain) — the 250 ms latch holds and every key change is demanded by a real table-version change. Token rotations (~13.5/s per owner) are 100% authoritative table mutations (services 75.9k, partitions 61k, replica_operations 30.7k, publications 28k, nodes 21.6k, storage_reservations 9.2k, node_endpoints 4.7k across 52 owners); non-semantic rotations 0 (transport fingerprint 54, owner-dep 3). This corrects the earlier inference of ~14 planning rotations/s/node, which came from first-differing-segment attribution in the A3 v1 key, not from a latch measurement.

FIRST LIVENESS BREAK (P1 on the FLOORED generation, not the exact token; publication is sound): every owner#1 rebuild lands CURRENT (35,240/35,240 across runs, 0 STALE, 0.17-0.25 ms each, 0 token rotations during builds); the reuse predicate rejects 100% of deferrals as token_rotated_after_current_build+floored_generation_advanced (29,700 of 29,729; live veto 29) because the floored generation — the cluster-wide 6-table latch key — rotates ~1/s and each rotation invalidates ALL ~30 (node x buildOptions-variant) completed records at once, which the owner refreshes one per macrotask drain (5-100 ms typical, 0.25-5 s under event-loop gaps); a hot seed variant is current for only part of each ~1.3 s window (rejected records aged 0.25-30 s; per-variant re-publish every 0.25-5 s; 122-132 publishes per variant vs 243 rotations), so per-read deferral is 37-74% (run variance), and the critical-topology settling gate's all-five-nodes conjunction on its 5 s pass almost never observes every node current (601/175 waits). Not P2 (publication works), not P4 (veto changed 29x), not P5 (writes ~13.5/s are real but latched to ~1/s; the scope of the currency, not the write rate, is the defect).

Repair direction (NOT started): the planning owner's floored currency is a whole-table cluster-wide over-approximation (the same class A3 removed from the evidence key) — scope it to the node's semantic inputs (the A3 content generation of the snapshot core + membership content + planning verdict content) so a write that cannot change node N's snapshot never invalidates N's record; and retire the 51 duplicate per-partition readiness services by injecting the coordinator's shared service (a separate bounded ownership defect that multiplies fan-out 52x and eats the drain budget). Do not loosen the settling gate, do not add wall-clock timeouts, do not touch clocks.
